slides.say: A circle with center O has a radius of ten centimeters. The highlighted arc A B is four pi centimeters long. What is alpha?
Let's use Understanding. We'll find which part of the circle the arc is. To do that, we compare the arc with the whole circumference.
We know the arc is four pi, and the radius is ten. So let's find the whole circumference. Two pi r is two pi times ten, which is twenty pi.
at: Two pi r is two pi times

slides.say: So the whole circle is twenty pi, and the arc is four pi. Four pi out of twenty pi is like four out of twenty, because the pi cancels. Four out of twenty is a fifth. So the arc is a fifth of the circle. Five arcs like it go all the way around.
at: Four pi out of twenty pi
Four out of twenty is a fifth

slides.say: And if the arc is a fifth of the circle, its central angle is also a fifth of the full turn. Three hundred sixty divided by five is seventy-two. So alpha is seventy-two degrees, choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: its central angle is also a fifth
